01 · Three type voices

Display for large titles and verdicts, text for the UI, and data — monospaced and tabular — for every number, date, amount and micro-label. Numbers never jitter.

The data face needs naming, and Menlo is the wrong answer

Menlo is Apple-only. On Android it falls back to the proportional default, and the one promise this voice exists to keep — numbers never jitter — breaks silently on the platform the project calls co-equal.

Recommendation: IBM Plex Mono, bundled. Genuinely tabular, open-licensed, ships on both platforms, and its warmth sits with the paper rather than against it. This sheet is set in it, so you are reading the proposal, not a description of it.

Uppercase is a style, not a string

The build currently uppercases the string itself in two places, which leaves nothing for a screen reader to strip. Micro-labels are authored in sentence case and transformed in the style layer — the accessibility label reads "Where it went", not "WHERE IT WENT".

Dynamic type

Every two-column construct on the sheets that follow reflows to one column at the largest sizes. The fact-row label column is not a fixed width — the build's 118 pt cap truncates where §H4 requires reflow.

02 · The Row

Icon well · title · one-line meta · trailing mono amount · date. One design, used in History, the car page's three recent, every Insights record list, and Home's Last fill.
Anatomy
Repsol Tarragona
6,9 L/100km · 378 km
35,75 €
12 Jul
Well — the domain hue. This is the whole colour job on a row.
Meta — leads with the derived value and its interval, never a bare number.
Amount — always ink. The well already said what kind of money it is.
Three laws the anatomy encodes
INV. 7 · THE FOLD RULE
A reading logged with a fill or a trip lives inside that record and never gets its own row — it still joins the trail. A deliberate manual reading always keeps its row. The single most common History bug class, and it is an invariant, not a preference.
INV. 17 · A TRIP IS DISTANCE
A trip's trailing figure is 232 km, never a euro amount. Its ≈costs are a share of money already counted, so they ride in the meta and on its record page — never in the money column.
INV. 16 · A NOTE IS NOT MONEY
No amount, ever, and it never joins a month whisper. On its record page the absence is stated where a reader would look for the number: "Note · not counted in totals."

The five fuel variants are one row design reading five different data situations — measured, partial, no odometer, missed-previous, money-only. None of them is styled as an error, and none apologises. That is the whole reason to draw them together: the degraded row must look like a row, not like a problem.

03 · Icon wells

One glyph per record type, used identically everywhere. An icon well — not a coloured bar, which is what the build ships today.
{{ w.iconLight }}
{{ w.iconDark }}
{{ w.name }}
{{ w.role }}
Glyphs here are placeholders

Standing in for the real thin-stroke set. What is not a placeholder is the count — eight glyphs, fixed — and which hue each wears. Both are decided; the drawing is not.

Three wells are ink, on purpose

Odometer, trip and note are not money, so their wells take the hairline surface and let the glyph identify them. This is what stops the ledger from reading as seven palettes.

The chooser reuses them exactly

Capture's six tiles wear the same eight glyphs at the same hues — money tiles coloured, the rest ink. A user who has seen a row already knows the tile.

04 · Chips and buttons

Three chip species that must never be confused: a filter fills with ink, an option washes with accent, a status chip is not tappable at all.
LIGHT
FILTER · SELECTED = INK-FILLED
All Fuel Service Expense
All is a chip, not a clear button — mutually exclusive with the rest, which are additive.
OPTION · SELECTED = ACCENT-WASHED
Petrol Diesel Electric Hybrid
The accent is the fuel hue — which is exactly right here, and a coincidence worth noticing rather than generalising.
STATUS · NOT TAPPABLE, LABELS ONLY
Mapfre 1.240/1.500 km Insurance in 16 days
180 km over Owned
A tappable status chip is hidden navigation with no back story. Facts, not warnings — and over-cap wears attention, never red.
BUTTONS · ONE PRIMARY PER SURFACE
Review Mark done Snooze +7 Delete this fill
Primary · secondary · ghost · destructive. Destructive is critical text on the ordinary surface — never a red fill. Minimum target 44 pt in every variant, including the ghost.
DARK
FILTER · SELECTED = INK-FILLED
All Fuel Service Expense
"Ink-filled" inverts with the theme — in dark, ink is the near-white, so the selected chip is the lightest object in the row.
OPTION · SELECTED = ACCENT-WASHED
Petrol Diesel Electric Hybrid
The wash is a dark tint of the accent, not the accent at low opacity — opacity over a warm ground goes grey.
STATUS · NOT TAPPABLE, LABELS ONLY
Mapfre 1.240/1.500 km Insurance in 16 days
180 km over Owned
The plum chip is the one place a domain hue carries type at chip size — so it takes the -text step, per sheet 01's rule.
BUTTONS · ONE PRIMARY PER SURFACE
Review Mark done Snooze +7 Delete this fill
The primary's label goes to the paper, not to white — a solid accent with white type on a warm dark ground reads as a notification, not as a button.

05 · Toasts, and the surface that never turns red

One at a time, app-level. Success 3 s · undo 6 s behind a draining hairline · error persists. Undo and Retry are the only actions that ride in a toast.
SUCCESS · 3 s · NO ACTION
✓ Done. Next one created for 16 July 2027.
UNDO · 6 s · DRAINING HAIRLINE
⌫ Reading deleted. Undo
The hairline is the state. It is why the surface never needs to turn a colour to tell you something is time-boxed.
ERROR · PERSISTS · ICON CARRIES IT
▪ Not syncing: your server didn't answer. Your records are safe on this device. Retry
A sentence, never a raw error string — and attention, not critical: a server that did not answer is a fact, and the records are fine.
§16 #8 — two quick deletes, and the answer I took

One-toast-at-a-time plus an in-memory undo closure means a second delete silently makes the first permanent. Following the wireframes' own recommendation rather than inventing a third option: the closures queue. The new toast supersedes visually, each closure survives its own 6 s, and the copy collapses — "2 records deleted." with one Undo that restores both. Still open for you: this is a recommendation, and it is logged as one.

06 · The three layer species

Push to go, sheet to do, fit to pick — and never two tall layers. Maximum depth anywhere: root → pushes → one task sheet → one fitted pick.
PUSHED PAGE · TAB BAR STAYS
‹ Garage Golf GTI
page body
HomeHistoryInsightsGarage
Back always means back. A pushed page never dismisses itself — it pops by path mutation only, which is the hard-won bug: dismiss() inside a pushed page eventually rebinds to a sheet and kills Back.
TASK SHEET · ONE TALL LAYER, NO TAB BAR
Discard Fill-up Save
task body
A sheet never presents a second tall surface. It continues by inline swap (the car form's ownership rows) or by pushing on its own internal stack (Settings does this, back-only, swipe-close disabled while pushed).
FITTED PICK · PARENT VISIBLE, NO SAVE
Cost ▾
‹ July 2026 · to date ▾ ›
Cost ✓
Fuel
Distance
Ownership
Applies on tap, closes itself, no Save button. Drawn with no title — §16 #11's recommendation: four rows say what they are, and "lens" never becomes user-facing vocabulary, which was the whole objection.

07 · Stat table, gauge, confirmation

The three constructs that carry most of Insights and every destructive act.
STAT TABLE · VERTICAL, ALWAYS
THE NUMBERS JULY
Average6,9 L/100km
Best · worst6,4 · 7,4
Last6,9 · 12 Jul
Cadence11 days · 378 km
Per fill28,4 L · 46,15 €
Verticals beat horizontal pills — Tester M's round-3 note. The label column is not fixed-width; at the largest text sizes each pair stacks.
GAUGE · FILL + TRACK + A SENTENCE
CAP CYCLE · 23 JUL – 22 AUG
1.240 / 1.760 km
1.500 cap + 260 carried over from June.
At your pace, ≈1.410 km by 22 August.
Under the cap.
1.840 / 1.760 km
1.500 cap + 260 carried over from June.
80 km over your pooled budget.
At your pace, ≈2.020 km by 22 August.
Over-cap fills attention, the overage is counted in text, and the pace line stays present tense. Never hidden, never red, nothing flashes. The denominator is the pooled budget — a gauge drawn against the bare 1.500 would flag a car that is still under budget.
CONFIRMATION · TYPED WHERE IT MUST BE
Delete this fill?
It leaves History and your averages, and the next fill's interval is measured again.
Keep it Delete
Remove Golf GTI?
This deletes the car, its records, reminders and documents. There is no undo.
Type Golf GTI to confirm
Cancel Remove
A car delete demands the car's name, not a generic word — "demands its name understood". Remove stays disabled until it matches, and a wrong entry says so rather than silently doing nothing, which is what the build does today.

08 · The chart grammar, and its table-first form

Charts are deliberately not installed. §D4's own escape hatch makes that honest rather than a compromise: a chart that cannot earn its headline and sentence is a stat table instead.

Each pair below is ships-now on the left and the target on the right. The left column is what sheets 04–07 draw, per your call. The right column is the grammar the marks must obey when the canvas arrives — same headline, same sentence, same period receipt, so gaining marks later is not an IA change.

The window's distance is measured from the last reading at or before it opens — 28 June here, not a July row. Labelling that row Anchor rather than First is the difference between a receipt and a number that cannot be checked. The projection anchors two months past today, never past the last reading.

Dashed tail, hollow endpoint, ≈ on the value and the date in the caption. Full locale format throughout — 92.388 km, never an abbreviated 92k.
The marks, fixed
Average = dashed hairline. Best = filled dot. Worst = hollow dot, attention. Projection = dashed tail + hollow endpoint, always ≈, dated in the caption. Ghost bars past the edges say "more history this way".
One series colour per chart
This is why sheet 01's fuel-vs-service luminance collision never bites: no chart shows two domain hues. The single exception labels every bar by name.
Max ~8 marks, labels that answer
The peak bar carries period + value; tapping any bar replaces that label and clears on data change. Line endpoints carry values beside the dots. A trend line needs ≥3 points to earn its space.
Ownership needs no canvas at all
A ledger card and a dot list, losing nothing. It is also the lens Tester M asked for by name — which makes it the one to build first if a real lens is wanted before the chart work.

09 · Motion, and targets

150 ms fades everywhere. Exactly one spring in the whole app. Reduce-motion gets fades only.

The one spring, and where it is not

The fuel-capture saved moment is the only spring in Koi. It is for the record landing, not for the user's behaviour — which is the difference between feedback and gamification.

page push / pop       150 ms fade + platform slide
row → record page      zoom transition from the row
state change on Home   150 ms fade — Home must not perform relief
toast in / out          150 ms fade
carousel page turn     native snap physics, edges rubber-band
capture success        one spring · ~2 s · auto-dismiss

Never

A streak. A badge. Confetti. A progress ring that fills for encouragement. A pulsing dot. A count-up animation on a number. A chart on Home. A red surface. An exclamation mark.

These are refusals, not omissions — the app never performs enthusiasm, and progress dots in the sparse fuel card teach rather than reward.

Targets

≥44 pt everywhere, rows are real buttons, and decorative glyphs are hidden from the screen reader. A chart exposes its headline + sentence as its accessible summary — which is the same thing the table-first build already renders, so accessibility arrives with the feature instead of as an overlay later.
Sheet 02 of 08. Everything from here is assembled out of exactly these parts — if a screen needs something that is not on this sheet, that is a finding about the screen, not a licence to draw a new control. Next: 03 the shell.
